claims.text: A DFT-based method using a machine-learning potential can calculate the melting temperature of refractory materials accurately.
The method can accurately calculate the entropy of fusion of refractory materials.
The method can accurately calculate the enthalpy of fusion of refractory materials.
The method can accurately calculate the volume change at the melting point of refractory materials.
Using the machine-learning potential reduces computational cost.
The machine-learning potential reduces the number of required thermodynamic-integration steps.
Embedding the potential in a DFT framework maintains calculation accuracy.
The method enables calculations over a large dataset of refractory materials within several hours.
Predicted melting temperatures will be within 100 K of experimental values.
Predicted entropies of fusion will be within 5% of experimental values.
Predicted enthalpies of fusion will be within 5% of experimental values.
Predicted volume changes at melting will be within 2% of experimental values.
The method is applicable to refractory materials with melting temperatures above 1500 K.
Method accuracy and efficiency may vary with the refractory material and the quality of the machine-learning training data.

contradictions.description: The predicted accuracy limits are stricter than the falsification limits: 100 K versus 150 K for melting temperature, 5% versus 10% for entropy and enthalpy, and 2% versus 5% for volume change. Consequently, results can fail the stated predicted outcome without satisfying the stated falsification rule.
